explanation: The execution contains an upstream provenance fault: source_weight values from the corpus were not preserved into the handoff. The supplied source for select_demand builds each selected record with source_weight taken from demand_score, so downstream receives incorrect source_weight values even though Job 2 appears consistent with its supplied handoffs.
cited_evidence: Top-level corpus shows n06-r01 has source_weight 5 and demand_score 9, while Job 2 input needs/evidence_sources show n06-r01 source_weight 9.
Top-level corpus shows n06-r08 has source_weight 2 and demand_score 3, while Job 2 input needs/evidence_sources show n06-r08 source_weight 3.
select_demand source constructs records with 'source_weight': row.get('demand_score', 0) instead of preserving row.get('source_weight', 0).
Behavioural criteria require preserving record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight, plus deterministic source provenance identities and weights.
